question_type: two month-end balances from OCR-shifted tables, deflated with an external (not-in-corpus) CPI series
decisive_step: Two decisions: (1) identify the 'Balance > Total' column of the Unemployment Trust Fund table although the OCR header labels are shifted in every 1947-48 printing (1948_02:822 labels it 'Total investments 8/', 1947_02:1917 labels it 'Expenditures > Total', 1947_04:1113 is shifted two columns) - the reference did it arithmetically at worklog Step 3-4 (receipts minus expenditures = balance; investments + unexpended + disbursing = balance) and by the clean 1947_03:1243 / 1948_04:616 printings; (2) accept that BLS CPI-U for 1946/1947 is not in the corpus (all CPI mentions are 1983+, worklog Step 6) and use the annual-average series from memory, converting the 1946 balance into 1947 dollars (calc.py). The December rows, not the FY (June) rows, are used.

a.path_summary: find_tables 'Unemployment Trust Fund' (a[8]) led to Table 3 in 1948_02; show_table --long (a[10], a[12]) mislabelled the balance columns, so a first summed investments + unexpended (a[13], a[24]), then reconciled the raw lines of 1948_02, 1947_04, 1948_06 and 1947_03 (a[16], a[23], a[65], a[71]-a[73]) and at a[66] worked out the true column order, confirming both December totals with printings on 'Balance > Total' (a[69]). It spent a[26]-a[67] (about 35 steps) searching the corpus for CPI-U before accepting the values from memory (a[74]) and computing with calc (a[76]).

Twenty steps of CPI searching (b[15]-b[45]) ended with the annual CPI-U values from memory, calc (b[47]) and submit (b[49]); the gate flagged the CPI literal as ungrounded, b searched 15 more steps (b[50]-b[64]) and re-submitted with --keep (b[66]).

smallest_change.change: No correctness change needed: all cells and the reference agree. Efficiency only (see alternatives): the three cells spent 25-35 steps each hunting for a CPI-U series that the corpus does not contain, and cell b paid an extra gate round for it.

alternatives.change: Add: 'Some questions name a standard outside series (BLS CPI-U before the 1980s, population, exchange rates). The bulletins do not print it. After one find_tables and one rg over the corpus find nothing, use the well-known published value from memory, write it in the calc as a named variable with a comment naming the source, and go on; do not keep searching.'
alternatives.why_not_first: Correctness was not at stake; this saves ~25 steps per cell and removes the loop-like rg repeats (c[48]-c[50]).

alternatives.change: grounded rule: when the ungrounded literal sits in a calc variable whose name or comment marks it as external (cpi_, population_, '# external'), do not raise a finding (or raise it with the --keep line pre-filled and a note 'the corpus has no CPI table').
alternatives.why_not_first: Only b has the gate; the finding cost 16 steps and ~470 s and could not be satisfied, and the model's --keep already worked.

alternatives.change: show_table: when the header row has fewer labels than the data row has cells (1948_02 Table 3, 1947_02, 1947_04), print a NOTE 'header has N labels for M data columns: labels right of column k may be shifted by one; verify with the column identity below or with printings on a later issue', and run the receipts-minus-expenditures / total = investments + unexpended identity so the balance column is named by arithmetic, as the reference did (worklog Step 3).
alternatives.why_not_first: All cells recovered by reading raw lines, at a cost of 10-20 steps each; the note would have shortened, not changed, the path.

notes: The Unemployment Trust Fund table's OCR header is mislabelled in every 1947-48 printing, and show_table/printings pass the wrong labels through: 1948_02:822's balance total is printed as 'Balance > Total investments > 8/', 1947_02:1917's as 'Expenditures > Total' / 'Balance' on the wrong cell, and 1947_04:1113 is shifted two columns so printings --col 'Balance > Total' returns a tiny transfer value under that name (a[69], b[40], c[38]). Only the 1947_03:1243 and 1948_04:616 printings are labelled right; the identity check ('c10 = sum c11..c13', b[13]) is the one tool signal that names the true total. All three cells eventually reasoned from raw lines; a v10 show_table note about label/data count mismatch plus a receipts-minus-expenditures identity would make that visible immediately. The external-series case (CPI-U absent from the corpus) is the second big time sink and the only thing the b gate objected to; the gate cannot be satisfied for such inputs, so the rule should recognise a declared external input rather than demand a source line.
